To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

co workers of a recipient of HR differentiation are likely to react positively by showing content with behavioural consequences toward their focal employee, when the recipient is highly committed to the organization, the recipient's contribution to the team is highly visible and the team is characterized by high social cohesion.
co workers react to HR differentiation with anger and contentment.

HR differentiation can be defined as a set of practices that are deliberately differentiating across employees to address their unique work needs and reward them for their unique input; co workers are more likely to react positively when they perceive that the focal employee's HR advantage is deserved and when the focal employee is a good team player; and co workers are more inclined to show anger when they perceive that HR differentiation is not deserved and when the team is characterized by high interdependence and high team identification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of HR differentiation on employees' co workers, and how these effects are moderated by contextual factors.
how the implementation of HR differentiation affects the well-being of co workers and the organization as a whole.
how co workers react when HR differentiation is implemented in their team and what contextual conditions affect such reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HR differentiation can be a double edged swords for the focal employee as well as the organization, as it may be perceived as unfair by co workers.
HR differentiation has the potential to increase the level of employee satisfaction, which in turn can lead to increased productivity.

the effects of HR differentiation on employees' well-being, performance, and turnover intentions are likely to be moderated by the extent to which co workers are content or angry about the HR differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HR differentiation can lead to both positive and negative outcomes, depending on how co workers interpret the fairness of HR differentiation and the context.
HR differentiation is a double edged sword.
we have conceptualized the consequences of HR differentiations for co workers and the context in which these consequences occur.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HR differentiation is likely to be a double edged-sword.
HR differentiation should be considered as a team level phenomenon and that the consequences of HR practices on co workers should be carefully considered when implementing them.
the consequences of HR practices are not confined to the recipients but can extend to co workers as well, who are likely to react in different ways depending on the contextual conditions.
